# Lazur: full product details for LLMs
# https://www.lazur.app/llms-full.txt
# Last updated: October 30, 2026

## Overview

Lazur is an AI buddy for Mac. It lives in the MacBook notch (or the top centre of the screen on Macs without one). You hold a key and talk; Lazur can see your screen when you ask, answers out loud, points at things by drawing on your screen, guides you through apps step by step, does everyday tasks on your Mac, runs longer jobs in the background and types for you in any app.

It is not a chat window: you don't copy, paste or describe your screen. It is not always listening: it only listens and looks while you hold its shortcut.

## Core features

### Ask about your screen (hold ⌥ ⌘)
Ask anything about what's in front of you ("what does this error mean?", "summarise this thread", "what's driving this chart?"). Lazur takes one screenshot at that moment, answers out loud, and doesn't store it.

### Pointing
"Where's the share button?" Lazur finds the exact element (using the Mac's accessibility tree and on-screen text) and draws a hand-drawn circle and label around it, including menu-bar icons with no text such as Control Center or Wi-Fi.

### Step-by-step guidance
"How do I turn on dark mode?" Lazur circles the first thing to click, waits for your click, looks at the new screen and circles the next step until you're done. It adapts if you click somewhere else.

### Everyday actions
Timers that tick in the notch (and ring until you stop them), Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume (Spotify or Music), opening apps and links, web search, running Shortcuts, clicking app menu items.

### Background jobs
Multi-step work such as research, comparisons or reading a feed runs as a background job in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. Jobs can use sites the user is already signed into, stop to ask before anything that can't be undone, and finish with a spoken summary and a full report. Routines (for example "always move new screenshots to a folder") run locally on the Mac.

### Dictation (hold fn)
Clean, punctuated text at the cursor in any app. Removes filler words, applies spoken corrections ("Friday, no, Thursday" becomes "Thursday"), formats lists. Includes snippets (say a short phrase, get saved text), Words (a personal dictionary for names and terms) and clipboard slots.

### Memory (from version 0.1.12)
Lazur remembers what the user asked it, what it answered and what it did (actions, background jobs, saved files), grouped into sessions and days, with one-line summaries and weekly and monthly notes. Ask "what were we debugging yesterday?", "what did I do with Priya last week?" or say "remember this" to save details from the screen. It links people, projects and topics across days and finds related words ("invoice" also finds "bill"). Kept on the Mac only, per account; never dictation, audio or screenshots. The Memory tab shows and searches everything and can delete any moment, session or day; Settings → Memory pauses it, excludes apps or erases it all.

### Saved files (from version 0.1.12)
Drag a file onto the notch to keep it in Lazur (a copy; the original stays where it was). Lazur reads its text on the Mac (PDFs, images via on-device text recognition, Word, RTF, text and code), so the user can ask about it later. Background jobs can attach a saved file to an upload field on a web form, asking before submitting. Files are listed in the Artifacts tab.

### Notch and app
Lazur's panel grows out of the notch. Hover it for jobs and status. Settings include cursor styles (Classic, Bubble, Halo, Sparkle), shortcuts, microphone and timer sound. Updates install automatically when the Mac is idle (from version 0.1.11).

## Pricing (October 2026)
- 3-day Pro trial for every new user, no credit card; starts on first app launch.
- Pro: $18/month, or $15/month billed annually. 150 AI actions a month, unlimited dictation.
- Power: $120/month, or $96/month billed annually. 1,000 AI actions a month, unlimited dictation.
- AI action = one request to Lazur (question, pointing, action, or background job). Dictation is not counted.
- Students can contact Lazur for a student offer.

## Platform
- macOS, Apple silicon and Intel builds.
- Needs Microphone, Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.
- Windows is planned; there is a waitlist on the download page.

## Privacy model
- Listens and captures the screen only while the user holds the shortcut.
- Audio, one screenshot, selected text, the frontmost app's name and local time are sent to AI providers to answer the request; Lazur does not store the audio or screenshot.
- Dictation audio is sent to speech-to-text providers and not stored.
- Content is not sold and not used to train AI models.
- Memory and saved files stay on the Mac. To write their one-line summaries, the start of a saved file's text and a finished session's text are sent to Lazur's servers and its AI provider, and not stored.
- Full policy: https://www.lazur.app/privacy

## How Lazur compares
- vs Clicky (HeyClicky): both are voice-first AI buddies for Mac that see the screen. Lazur lives in the notch and emphasises drawing on screen, step-by-step guidance, everyday Mac actions and dictation; Clicky sits beside the cursor and emphasises agents and SaaS connectors. https://www.lazur.app/blog/lazur-vs-heyclicky
- vs Meta's Muse for Mac: Muse is a task agent working across files and Apple apps; Lazur is a buddy for live help in the app you're using. https://www.lazur.app/blog/lazur-vs-muse-for-mac
- vs ChatGPT / Claude desktop apps: those live in a window and need you to share or describe your screen; Lazur works on top of any app and acts on the Mac.
- vs dictation apps (Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, Aqua Voice): Lazur includes full dictation but is mainly an assistant that answers, points and acts. https://www.lazur.app/compare

## FAQ
- What is Lazur? An AI buddy for Mac that lives in the notch: it sees your screen when you ask, talks back, points at things, gets things done and types for you.
- Is it always listening? No. Only while you hold ⌥ ⌘ (ask) or fn (dictate).
- Does it work in every app? Yes, on top of any Mac app, including web apps.
- How much is it? A free 3-day Pro trial, then Pro at $18/month or Power at $120/month.
- Does it update itself? Yes, from version 0.1.11.
- Does Lazur remember things? Yes, from version 0.1.12: past sessions on your Mac, which you can search, pause or erase.
